en.p: There are 6 cards; on the front of each, one of the natural numbers from 1 to 6 is written, and on the back of each, 0 is written. As shown in the figure, for each natural number $k$ at most 6, the cards are placed so that the natural number $k$ shows in the $k$th position.

en.fig: See the original for the figure.

en.p: Using these 6 cards and one die, the following trial is performed.

box: Roll the die once; if the number rolled is $k$,
flip the card in the $k$th position over once and put it back in its place.

en.p: After repeating this trial 3 times, given that the sum of all numbers showing on the 6 cards is even, the probability that the die showed 1 exactly once is $\dfrac{q}{p}$. Find the value of $p+q$. (Here $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime natural numbers.) [4 points]
